en.title: The Black Tapes Podcast Becomes MGM+ Series with Nikolaj Coster-Waldau
en.summary: The chilling paranormal investigation podcast that captivated millions is getting a new life as an eight-episode series on MGM+. Game of Thrones alum Nikolaj Coster-Waldau is set to star as the enigmatic Dr. Richard Strand.
en.body:
Hold the phone! The unnerving world of **The Black Tapes** podcast is officially making the leap to television. MGM+ has announced an eight-episode series based on the critically acclaimed 2015 horror podcast created by Terry Miles and Paul Bae. Stepping into the shoes of the brilliant but haunted paranormal investigator, Dr. Richard Strand, will be none other than **Nikolaj Coster-Waldau**, known to many for his iconic role as Jaime Lannister in **Game of Thrones**. The series, also titled **The Black Tapes**, is slated to begin filming in January 2027, bringing the podcast's unique blend of dread and mystery to a new audience.

The show's narrative promises to stay true to its source material. Dr. Richard Strand, a psychiatrist shrouded in a mysterious past, joins forces with the tenacious and driven scientist Alex Regan. Together, they aim to debunk seemingly supernatural occurrences: hauntings, possessions, inexplicable disappearances, and chilling local legends, all documented on the infamous "black tapes." However, as their investigation deepens, Strand and Regan begin to unearth a terrifying occult underworld lurking just beneath the surface of our reality. Their quest for truth escalates into a desperate race to unravel a centuries-old apocalyptic conspiracy that threatens everything they thought they knew.

This adaptation is in capable hands, with original creators Terry Miles and Paul Bae attached as writers and executive producers. "I was an early and passionate fan of The Black Tapes podcast," shared John Rogers, who is executive producing the effort with his partner Jennifer Court at Kung Fu Monkey Productions and Kearie Peak at Peak Pictures. "It’s a unique blend of truly unsettling horror and puzzling mysteries that we believe will translate powerfully to the screen." The podcast itself garnered a massive following for its immersive storytelling, presented as a true-crime documentary series that blurred the lines between fiction and reality, leaving listeners questioning what was real.

## A Deep Dive into the Darkness

For the legions of fans who were enthralled by the slow-burn dread and intricate plotting of **The Black Tapes** podcast, this news is a cause for significant excitement. The podcast's success was a testament to the power of audio storytelling to create deeply unsettling atmospheres and compelling mysteries. Its narrative structure, which often left listeners grappling with ambiguity and unresolved questions, fostered a vibrant online community dedicated to dissecting every clue and theorizing about the overarching plot. The transition to a visual medium, especially with an actor of **Coster-Waldau**'s caliber, offers the potential to amplify the horror and expand the lore, bringing the occult world and its ancient conspiracy to life in a visceral new way. The community will be eagerly watching to see how the series captures the podcast's signature tone and whether it can maintain the suspense that made the original so addictive.

## What's Next for the Tapes

With filming set to commence in January 2027, fans can anticipate further casting announcements and production updates in the coming months. The involvement of the original creators suggests a faithful adaptation that will likely satisfy long-time listeners while also drawing in new viewers drawn to **Nikolaj Coster-Waldau** and the promise of a compelling supernatural thriller. The exact release date on MGM+ has not yet been announced, but the production timeline indicates a potential premiere in late 2027 or early 2028.

MGM+ is turning the popular 2015 Black Tapes horror podcast by Terry Miles and Paul Bae into an eight-episode series starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau ( Game of Thrones ) as the supernatural investigator, Dr. Richard Strand. The show will also be called The Black Tapes and will begin filming in January 2027. Here’s the official description of the series, which hews closely to the podcast: Dr. Richard Strand (Coster-Waldau), a brilliant psychiatrist with a mysterious past, teams with the obsessed, relentless scientist Alex Regan to debunk paranormal cases of hauntings, possessions, disappearances, and sinister legends—the infamous black tapes. But as Strand and Regan unravel the secrets of these events, they uncover a hidden occult world behind our own and must unravel a centuries-old apocalyptic conspiracy.  Miles and Bae are also involved in the TV show as writers and executive producers. “I was an early and passionate fan of  The Black Tapes  podcast,” said John Rogers, who is executive producing the effort with his partner Jennifer Court at Kung Fu Monkey Productions and Kearie Peak at Peak Pictures. “It’s a unique blend of truly unsettling horror and puzzle-box conspiracy mystery. With Paul and Terry not just executive producing, but also in the writers’ room, we have a chance to both bring  The Black Tapes  to a new generation of genre fans and deepen and expand the mythos in ways that will surprise long-time supernatural horror fans.” No news yet on who will star as Coster-Waldau’s partner, Alex Regan, though with production starting in the new year, we’ll likely find out sooner rather than later.
